newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil shares unmoved despite fuel crisis.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil shares unmoved despite fuel crisis.

text.p: Oil shares remained steady on the Nigerian stock market on Monday as the fuel crisis that began last week showed no sign of ending.

The all share index was not updated due to technical problems. Traders said the market remained driven by interest in blue chip stocks in banking, conglomerates and food and beverages as traders decided to overlook the oil stocks.

"Dealers were unrelenting in their decision to shun the oil marketers until the fuel supply situation is normalised," one analyst said. "They hope that way, those in authority would act to end the crisis that is crippling business."
Motorists and commuters said on Monday that the fuel shortages that gripped the commercial capital Lagos last week was still on and had spread to neighbouring towns.
Shares of Lever Brothers moved 15 kobo to 25.40 naira, while PZ Industries rose five kobo to 25.70 naira.
Among food shares, Nestle was up 50 kobo to 67.00 naira on increasing demand.
Banks shares also strengthened on growing interest. First Bank led the pack, closing at 18.25 naira, up by 25 kobo, while Union Bank was up at 15.50 naira.
Nigerian Breweries rose 30 kobo to 19.05 naira, showing investors had completely mopped up excess shares that depressed the price for much of last year.

Tyremakers Dunlop added 20 kobo to 13.10 naira, while Industrial Gases surged to 9.00 naira, gaining 25 kobo. But dwindling fortunes at stationery firm Thomas Wyatt forced a 10 kobo drop to 4.70 naira. National Salt Co also fell 10 kobo to 6.10 naira.
